mods.name: Villager Chatter
mods.description: Villagers say AI-generated, situation-aware lines in speech bubbles, chat with you in the trading screen, and react to raids, bells and bedtime. Runs a small AI on your own computer, no account or setup.

releases.notes:
Also submitted to [Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/mod/villager-chatter) (waiting for review).

### New
- **In-game settings.** Open them from Mod Menu's Configure button (Mod Menu is optional) or type `/villagerchatter settings`. Chattiness, small talk, trade conversations, bubbles/chat/both, bubble size, villager sounds, mood particles, AI on/off, AI files folder, and Reset to Defaults.
- **Villager sounds.** Every line comes with the villager's own "hrmm": a happy one for good news, a grumpy one when they're upset, scared or woken up.
- **One AI folder for all your instances.** The model now lives in `~/Library/Application Support/VillagerChatter/` (macOS), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\VillagerChatter\` (Windows) or `~/.local/share/villagerchatter/` (Linux/SteamOS). Your existing download is moved there automatically on first launch, no re-download.
- Turning the AI off in the settings frees its memory; turning it back on restarts it.
- Mod icon in Mod Menu.

### Install / upgrade
Remove the old `villagerchatter-*.jar` from `mods` and drop in `villagerchatter-0.10.0.jar` (below).

Tested on macOS (Apple Silicon). Needs Fabric Loader for 26.3 + Fabric API, Java 25.

- **Waking a villager isn't an attack anymore.** Punch a sleeping villager awake and it's grumpy ("Five more minutes..."), but it doesn't count as a hit or hold a grudge.
- **Nitwits, unemployed villagers and kids talk now.** They have nothing to trade, so right-clicking them used to just get a head shake. Now they say something that fits (the nitwit knows it's a nitwit; the jobless one is looking for a workstation).

releases.notes:
Villagers now react to what's happening in their village.

## New
- **Raids:** when the first wave arrives, nearby villagers panic. When it ends, they celebrate a win or mourn a loss.
- **The bell:** ring the village bell and a nearby villager reacts.
- **Bedtime:** villagers sometimes mutter a goodnight as they climb into bed (only when you're close).
- Every reaction uses the AI when it's ready and falls back to hand-written lines otherwise. Each villager reacts at most once every 10 s, and only when a player is within 32 blocks.

## Install / upgrade
1. Fabric Loader for 26.3 + [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api)
2. **Remove the old `villagerchatter-*.jar`** from `mods`, then drop in `villagerchatter-0.9.0.jar` (below)
3. The AI model you already downloaded is reused, so there's no new 2.5 GB download.

## Requirements
- Java 25, ~3 GB free RAM and ~2.6 GB disk for the AI
- Tested on macOS (Apple Silicon) and SteamOS (Linux, Steam Machine). Windows builds are wired up; reports welcome!

The jar is built by GitHub Actions from this tag; a `.sha256` checksum file is attached next to it.

releases.notes:
First public release of **Villager Chatter**, a Fabric mod for **Minecraft 26.3** where villagers talk using a small AI model that runs **entirely on your computer**.

## Install
1. Fabric Loader for 26.3 + [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api)
2. Drop `villagerchatter-0.8.0.jar` (below) into your `mods` folder
3. Launch. On first run the mod downloads its AI (~2.5 GB, one time). Villagers use simple lines until chat says **"Villagers are now fully awake."**

## What's in it
- AI speech bubbles that fit each villager's job, biome, time, weather and danger, with vanilla mood particles
- Conversations in the trading screen: villager line + 3 AI reply options + "Let's just trade." (hover for full text)
- Villagers know their real trades, remember you (trades, hits, reputation), react to trades and to getting punched
- Villagers chat with each other
- Built-in AI: llama.cpp (pinned build b11242) + Qwen3-4B, SHA-256 verified, local-only (127.0.0.1), GPU when available (Metal / Vulkan, CPU fallback). Ollama optional via `backend=ollama`.

## Requirements
- Java 25 (Minecraft 26.x default), ~3 GB free RAM and ~2.6 GB disk for the AI
- Tested on macOS (Apple Silicon) and SteamOS (Linux, Steam Machine). Windows builds are wired up; reports welcome!

See the [README](https://github.com/NotEnxvinity/VillagerChatter#readme) for config options. The jar is built by GitHub Actions from this tag; a `.sha256` checksum file is attached next to it.
